typingTest.title: Typing Test
typingTest.description: Check Korean keystrokes, English WPM, and accuracy, then choose completed-practice sections around mistakes for separate review.

rules.title: How speed is counted
items: Korean speed = correct keystrokes (jamo) per minute, the same way Hancom Typing counts.
닭 = ㄷ·ㅏ·ㄹ·ㄱ is 4 keystrokes; double final consonants count as 2.
과 = ㄱ·ㅗ·ㅏ is 3 keystrokes; compound vowels count as 2.
Tense consonants (ㄲ ㄸ ㅃ ㅆ ㅉ) and ㅒ ㅖ count as 1 (Shift is not counted). Spaces and punctuation count as 1.
English WPM treats 5 correct characters as one word, per minute.
Accuracy counts every character you ever got wrong, even if you fixed it.
The syllable you are still composing is never marked wrong; it is shown with a blue underline.

howTo.title: How to use
items: Choose Daily, Short, Long, Timed or Custom text. For custom text, review the preview and apply it with Start with this text.
Measurement starts when you type the first character in the practice field. Editing the draft field does not start it.
Correct characters turn dark, errors have a red underline, and a composing syllable has a blue underline.
See results when you finish the text or a standard timed session ends. Custom-text results do not enter standard records or daily statistics.
Standard practice supports image and link sharing. Custom text only copies a result summary without the passage and does not create a same-passage share link.
In Practice missed sections below the completed result, select a candidate and choose Practice this section. Retrying or closing the section keeps the original result and custom-text draft.

speed.title: Grades (Korean KPM · English WPM)
items: Beginner: under 100 · under 20 WPM
Intermediate: 200-299 · 30-39 WPM (adult average about 250 · 40 WPM)
Advanced: 300-399 · 40-59 WPM
Legend: 600+ · 100+ WPM

whatIs.title: What is the Typing Test?
whatIs.description: Practice Korean or English with four standard modes or your own text. After completion, choose sections containing committed mistakes for separate review. Review preserves the original passage, result, and records and shows section accuracy and error-position count separately.

tips.title: Tips to Improve Your Typing
items: Focus on accuracy before speed. Reducing typos leads to faster long-term improvement than rushing and hitting errors.

Maintain the home row position (left hand on ASDF / ㅁㄴㅇㄹ, right hand on JKL; / ㅓㅏㅣ;, index fingers on the bumped F (ㄹ) and J (ㅓ) keys). Keeping fingers close to the home row reduces travel distance and naturally increases speed.
Practicing 10–15 minutes daily is more effective than a single long session. Muscle memory is built through consistent repetition.

items.q: What is the average Korean typing speed for an adult?
items.a: The average adult types around 200–300 keystrokes per minute (타수). 300–400+ keystrokes/min is considered fast, and 600+ matches this tool's top 'Legend' grade. There is no official standard, so treat these as rough guides.

items.q: What is the difference between WPM and keystrokes per minute?
items.a: WPM (Words Per Minute) is an English-centric metric counting words (standardized to 5 characters). Korean typing is traditionally measured in keystrokes per minute. Roughly, 60 WPM in English feels similar in effort to about 300 keystrokes/min in Korean.

Recent standard-practice results are saved in browser local storage. Custom passages and results stay in memory for this visit, are excluded from standard records and daily statistics, and are not added to the URL. Copy a custom-result summary if needed. Review practice also does not save passages or results or add them to standard records.

After practice ends, committed-input error positions identify sections separated by whitespace. A whitespace error includes both neighboring sections, and corrected mistakes remain eligible. Untyped text after a timed session is excluded. This is not grammar analysis or a diagnosis of the mistake.

items.q: Does review practice count toward my best score?
items.a: No. It shows completion, accuracy, and error-position count for the selected section without changing the original result, best records, or daily statistics. Original whitespace and punctuation remain, with sections up to 1,000 characters. Choose each next section yourself; review text is not added to URLs or stored records.

custom.title: Practice your own text
custom.switchNotice: Switching practice modes ends the current attempt. Your custom draft and confirmed passage stay on this page and are separate from standard practice records.
custom.description: Paste a passage, review the normalized preview, then practice. Your draft and passage stay in this page's memory and are not saved to records or shared URLs.
custom.normalization: Line breaks and tabs become spaces, repeated spaces become one, and leading/trailing spaces are removed. Your original draft is kept.
custom.previewEmpty: Enter a draft to preview the normalized passage.
custom.tooShort: The normalized passage must contain at least {min} characters.
custom.tooLong: The normalized passage can contain up to {max} characters. Shorten your draft; it will not be automatically truncated.
custom.nextLanguage: Speed unit for the next attempt
custom.languageHint: Korean uses the existing two-set jamo keystroke rules. English counts five correct characters as one word. Exact keyboard input counts for other writing systems are not guaranteed. This choice applies when you start the next attempt.
custom.replaceWarning: Applying a new passage ends the current attempt and starts over. Editing the draft alone leaves the current attempt unchanged.
custom.replaceCurrent: Replace current attempt and start this text
custom.confirmedHint: The timer starts with your first input. Draft edits do not change this passage.
custom.inputHint: Pasting and dropping are disabled here. Korean input completes after composition is committed. Press Esc to restart the same passage.
custom.resultScope: Custom passages vary in difficulty, so results are not compared with general averages or rankings. They do not count toward best scores, daily attempts, streaks or recent records.
custom.copyPrivacy: This summary does not include your passage or a link that opens the same passage.
custom.leaveHint: Switching to another practice mode clears the running timer and input. Your draft and confirmed passage stay while you remain on this page.

copyRecovery.failed: Automatic copying failed. Select the summary below and copy it manually, or use the copy button to retry.
copyRecovery.hint: This summary is read-only. Select it and use your device's copy command.
copyRecovery.selectionFailed: Automatic selection failed. Long-press or drag within the summary to select it manually.

review.title: Practice missed sections
review.description: Choose a word or the context around a missed space from your completed passage for a short practice.
review.scope: Sections use positions that were wrong in committed input, including corrected mistakes. Untyped text and unfinished IME input are excluded.
review.noErrors: There are no committed mistakes to practice.
review.spaceHint: Words are separated by whitespace. A missed space includes the words on both sides. Type the punctuation and spacing as shown.
review.tooLong: This section exceeds {max} characters and cannot start. Its text will not be shortened automatically.
review.replaceHint: Starting another section replaces only this practice attempt. Your original result and manuscript draft stay unchanged.
review.failed: This section could not be opened. Choose a section from the current result again.
review.unavailable: Practice sections could not be prepared for this result. Your original result and records are unchanged.
review.inputHint: Paste and drop are disabled. Enter does not add a line; Esc closes this practice. IME input is handled after composition ends.
review.resultScope: This result covers only this short section. It does not change your original result, best score, recent history or daily attempts.
